epic_title: Filename formats, date parsing, week numbers, locale
summary: This epic owns the two-way conversion between a date+granularity and a filename: generating a filename (including week tokens in the format field) from a date, and parsing an existing filename back into a date, deciding when that counts as a match. It also owns week numbering, week-start day, and locale, and validating a format string before it is saved. It hands NOTE the naming rules NOTE uses to look up, create and index files; NOTE decides what happens once a match (or collision) is found. It hands TPL the day-of-week resolution mechanism that TPL's note-body tokens also rely on, but owns only the filename-format-field half of the token syntax. SET owns where the format string lives and its settings UI; this epic owns only whether a given string is valid.

stories.title: Week-relative tokens in the filename format follow the configured week start
stories.story: As someone naming weekly notes with per-weekday tokens, I want {{monday:DD.MM}} and its six siblings to resolve to the date that falls in my own configured week rather than a fixed Monday-first week, so that the filename always names the days of the week I actually see everywhere else in the plugin.
stories.rationale: The current implementation is documented as respecting the week-start setting but hard-codes ISO Monday-first weeks instead, so filenames can silently name the wrong day.

acceptance_criteria.given: a weekly note whose own date is a Sunday and the configured week start is Monday
acceptance_criteria.when: the filename format contains a {{monday:fmt}} token
then: the token resolves to the Monday that begins the same week as the note's date, six days before that Sunday
the resolved date is rendered using the format given after the colon

acceptance_criteria.given: the same weekly note whose own date is that Sunday, but the configured week start is Sunday instead of Monday
acceptance_criteria.when: the filename format contains the same {{monday:fmt}} token
then: the token resolves to the Monday that ends the same week as the note's date, one day after that Sunday
this resolved date is a different calendar date, seven days later, than the one produced under a Monday week start for the same note

acceptance_criteria.given: a format string containing tokens for all seven weekday names, mixing upper and lower case
acceptance_criteria.when: the filename is generated for a weekly note
then: each token resolves to that weekday's date within the note's own configured week
weekday name matching in the token is case-insensitive

acceptance_criteria.given: a format string configured for a granularity other than week contains a weekday token such as {{monday:fmt}}
acceptance_criteria.when: the filename is generated
then: the token is left unresolved as literal text, because a weekday-within-the-week has no meaning for a note that is not a week

decisions.title: Week-based tokens and week numbers follow the configured week-start day
decisions.decision: The user's 'Start week on' setting is authoritative for week numbering and for the {{monday:fmt}}..{{sunday:fmt}} tokens, in both the filename format field and the note body. ISO week numbering is not hard-coded. The two surfaces must resolve the same weekday to the same date for the same setting.
decisions.rationale: The existing documentation already promises this and the code contradicts it. Keeping the promise is the smaller change and the honest one. In this vault the setting is Monday-first, so ISO and configured agree today and no existing note is affected.

stories.title: Month and week layout follow the configured week start
stories.story: As someone viewing a month of notes, I want each week's row to start on my configured week-start day and always show a complete 6-week grid, so that the week numbers and day columns match how I think about weeks.
stories.rationale: The grid math must key off the user's actual week-start setting rather than a value that is silently ignored, or the grid disagrees with every other week-aware feature in the plugin.

acceptance_criteria.given: the configured week start is Monday
acceptance_criteria.when: the grid for a given month is computed
then: every week row begins on a Monday
the grid contains exactly 6 rows of 7 days, including any leading days from the previous month and trailing days from the next month needed to fill the first and last rows

acceptance_criteria.given: the configured week start is Sunday, for the same month as AC-FMT-02.1
acceptance_criteria.when: the grid is computed
then: every week row begins on a Sunday instead
the specific dates assigned to each row differ from the Monday-start grid whenever the 1st of the month falls between Sunday and Monday in the two conventions

acceptance_criteria.given: a month whose 1st day of the month is itself the configured week-start day, so the month's own days would otherwise fit in 5 rows
acceptance_criteria.when: the grid is computed
then: the grid still contains exactly 6 rows of 7 days, padded with a full extra row of the following month's dates

acceptance_criteria.given: the month grid is computed for a displayed month
acceptance_criteria.when: the computation runs
then: the Moment instance representing the displayed month passed in by the caller is not mutated

stories.title: Locale and week-start settings govern weekday names and week numbers everywhere, live
stories.story: As someone who works in Polish and starts the week on Monday, I want every weekday name and week number the plugin shows or writes into a filename to follow my configured locale and week-start day consistently, so that I never have to translate or recompute dates by hand.
stories.rationale: The old implementation mutates locale globally once at load, loses changes until a full reload, and has a live setting-UI bug that writes the locale choice to the wrong key; this story defines the correct, live-updating, user-visible contract instead.

acceptance_criteria.given: the locale setting is set to Polish
acceptance_criteria.when: any weekday name, month name, or week number is rendered by the plugin, in the calendar, a filename, or a template token
then: Polish weekday and month names are used

acceptance_criteria.given: a week-start day is configured
acceptance_criteria.when: any week-based computation runs anywhere in the plugin, including the calendar grid, filename week tokens, and week-number resolution
then: all of them use the same configured week-start day
no feature is left using a different, hard-coded week-start convention than the others

acceptance_criteria.given: the plugin is already running and a note is open
acceptance_criteria.when: the user changes the locale or the week-start setting, without disabling and re-enabling the plugin or reloading Obsidian
then: the next date rendered anywhere in the plugin reflects the new setting immediately

acceptance_criteria.given: no locale override is configured
acceptance_criteria.when: the plugin resolves which locale to use
then: it falls back to Obsidian's own configured display language

acceptance_criteria.given: a locale value is stored that the date library does not recognise
acceptance_criteria.when: the plugin resolves which locale to use
then: it falls back to a default locale rather than leaving weekday names blank or throwing an error

stories.title: Parse a filename back into a date, honouring nested folders and an opt-in prefix fallback
stories.story: As someone who already has years of periodic notes on disk, I want the plugin to recognise which date and granularity each filename represents, even when the note lives in a dated subfolder or carries an extra descriptive suffix, so that my existing notes keep working after I switch to this plugin.
stories.rationale: Two independent old implementations of this exact behaviour exist and disagree; this story is the single specification the rewrite must follow so an existing vault keeps recognising its own notes.

acceptance_criteria.given: a granularity's configured format contains a folder separator, such as a year folder followed by a full date
acceptance_criteria.when: a file's full relative path exactly matches what that format would produce for some date
then: the file is recognised as an exact match for that granularity and date

acceptance_criteria.given: a note was originally created under a nested format but has since been moved so that only its filename, not its folder, matches the format's final segment
acceptance_criteria.when: the plugin resolves notes for that granularity
then: the file is still recognised, matched against its filename alone rather than its full path

acceptance_criteria.given: a filename does not exactly match the configured format for a granularity, but starts with what that format would produce for some date, followed by extra descriptive text
acceptance_criteria.when: prefix matching is disabled for that granularity, which is the default
then: the file is not recognised as a note for that period

acceptance_criteria.given: the same filename and format as AC-FMT-04.3, but prefix matching is enabled for that granularity
acceptance_criteria.when: the plugin resolves notes for that granularity
then: the file is recognised as a note for that date, as an inexact (prefix) match rather than an exact one

acceptance_criteria.given: a weekly format includes both a week-number token and a month or day token
acceptance_criteria.when: a filename is parsed against that format, whether the eventual match is exact or a prefix match
then: the week number encoded in the filename takes priority over any conflicting month or day fragment
this priority is applied the same way regardless of whether the match found is exact or a prefix match

acceptance_criteria.given: the vault already contains 219 daily notes named in the pattern "YYYY-MM-DD, dddd", 60 weekly notes named "YYYY-Wnn, DD.MM - DD.MM", 21 monthly notes named "YYYY-MM Month", and 25 monthly-work notes named "YYYY-MM Month - Work"
acceptance_criteria.when: the matching format strings are configured for each granularity and the vault is scanned
then: every one of these existing notes is recognised as the note for its date and granularity

acceptance_criteria.given: 7 daily notes exist in an older bare "YYYY-MM-DD.md" shape that predates the vault's current daily format
acceptance_criteria.when: the current format "YYYY-MM-DD, dddd" is configured, with prefix matching left at its default of disabled
then: these 7 files are not recognised as daily notes, matching the vault's behaviour before this rewrite rather than introducing a new gap

acceptance_criteria.given: two different files in the vault both resolve to the same date and granularity, one as an exact match and one as a prefix match
acceptance_criteria.when: the plugin looks up the note for that period
then: the exact match is treated as the note for that period
the prefix-matched file is not silently treated as an equally valid alternative for the same period

decisions.title: Candidate formats are tried in declaration order, and that order is documented
decisions.decision: When more than one candidate format validly matches the same file, the first in declaration order wins. The order is defined and documented rather than incidental.
decisions.rationale: Today the winner depends on an unspecified list order, so the same vault can resolve differently after an unrelated change. Any deterministic rule beats that; declaration order is the one a user can predict.

decisions.title: Week-number disambiguation applies whenever a day token is present
decisions.decision: The rule that separates a week number from a month-or-day value applies when the format carries a day token, whether or not it also carries a month token.
decisions.rationale: The narrower variant only triggered when both were present, so a format like DD slipped through and parsed as a week number. The wider rule catches the case the narrow one was written to catch.

stories.title: Validate a format string before it is saved
stories.story: As someone editing the filename format for a granularity, I want to be warned before saving a format that is illegal, cannot be told apart from other dates, or cannot survive being moved out of its folder, so that I do not silently lose the ability to find my own notes.
stories.rationale: A format that looks reasonable can still be unusable for its granularity; catching this at save time is cheaper than discovering it once notes already exist under it.

acceptance_criteria.given: a format string contains a character that cannot appear in a filename on the user's operating system, or resolves to a reserved filename
acceptance_criteria.when: the format is validated
then: it is rejected with an error before it can be saved

acceptance_criteria.given: a format string, applied to the current date and parsed back, does not return to the same date, or omits enough of the year, month, or day that many distinct dates would produce the same filename (for example, a day format of only "DD")
acceptance_criteria.when: the format is validated
then: the user is warned that the format cannot uniquely identify a note

acceptance_criteria.given: a format contains a folder separator, and the portion of the format after the last separator is on its own missing enough of the day, month, or year to identify a specific day
acceptance_criteria.when: the format is validated
then: the user is warned that a note moved out of its dated subfolder would no longer be recognised
the warning includes a workaround the user can apply

acceptance_criteria.given: an empty format string is entered for a granularity
acceptance_criteria.when: the format is validated
then: it is rejected as invalid rather than silently falling back to a hidden default

decisions.title: Format warnings inform, they do not block
decisions.decision: A format flagged as fragile or non-identifying shows a warning the user can read and dismiss. The value still saves.
decisions.rationale: The check is a heuristic. A user with a deliberate nested-path scheme should not be locked out by it, and a blocked save gives them nowhere to go.

stories.title: Canonical identity for a date and granularity
stories.story: As the system matching notes and calendar cells to periods, I want a single date and granularity to always produce the same canonical identity, so that two references to "this week" or "this day" are recognised as the same period regardless of the exact time of day carried by the underlying date value.
stories.rationale: Every lookup and duplicate-detection path in the plugin needs a stable way to say two dates mean the same period; this is the shared foundation the rest of FMT and NOTE build on.

acceptance_criteria.given: two date values representing different times of day on the same calendar day
acceptance_criteria.when: the day-granularity identity is computed for both
then: both produce the identical identity value

acceptance_criteria.given: a date value is passed in to compute an identity
acceptance_criteria.when: the identity is computed
then: the original date value is not mutated by the computation

acceptance_criteria.given: the same date value, but two different granularities such as day and the week containing that date
acceptance_criteria.when: identities are computed for each granularity
then: the two identities are different values
a day-note and a week-note covering the same date are never confused with each other because of this

acceptance_criteria.given: no granularity is specified when requesting an identity
acceptance_criteria.when: the identity is computed
then: it defaults to the day-granularity identity for that date

stories.title: Resolve which date and granularity an open file represents, day before week
stories.story: As someone with a note open, I want the plugin to recognise it as a specific day's or week's note by its filename, preferring the most specific granularity, so that the calendar highlights the exact cell for the note I am looking at.
stories.rationale: Highlighting the active note on the calendar depends on resolving its date correctly and consistently, without a day-note ever being mistaken for a week-note or vice versa.

acceptance_criteria.given: a file's name matches a valid daily-note filename
acceptance_criteria.when: its date identity is resolved
then: it is recognised as that day's note

acceptance_criteria.given: a file's name does not match a valid daily-note filename, but does match a valid weekly-note filename
acceptance_criteria.when: its date identity is resolved
then: it is recognised as that week's note

acceptance_criteria.given: a file's name matches neither a valid daily-note nor a valid weekly-note filename
acceptance_criteria.when: its date identity is resolved
then: no identity is returned, and the file is not treated as a periodic note for either granularity

acceptance_criteria.given: a file matches a daily or weekly format and its identity is resolved
acceptance_criteria.when: that identity is compared against the identity produced for the same date anywhere else in the plugin, such as the calendar grid
then: the two identities are equal, so cross-feature comparisons of the same date always agree

decisions.title: A file is the note for a period only when its folder matches too
decisions.decision: Recognising a file as a periodic note requires both the filename to match the granularity's format and the file to sit under that granularity's configured folder. Filename alone is not sufficient. No vault-wide loose fallback exists.
decisions.rationale: Today only the basename is checked, so two same-named files in different folders resolve identically, and an unrelated file whose name loosely resembles a date is cached as a periodic note. This also closes ICE-07, the icebox entry marked do-not-rebuild.

notes: Rival implementation decision: US-FMT-04 adopts the 'try every candidate format' structure (the one that already expands nested-path formats into a full-path and a basename-only candidate), because that structure is required anyway to support nested folder formats. Layered on top, it keeps the week-number-vs-month/day disambiguation from the single-format implementation, but applies it consistently to both the exact-match and the prefix-match branch, fixing an inconsistency present in the old single-format implementation (which only disambiguated on its exact-match branch). The undecided residue (candidate tie-break order, and how narrowly the disambiguation rule is scoped) is listed in US-FMT-04's open_questions.

pn:loose-date-parsing-fallback-global (a vault-wide loose date guess when no configured format matches at all) is icebox, not part of this epic; US-FMT-04's failure paths intentionally stop at 'not recognised' rather than falling back to a global guess.

forks:weekly-note-prefix-match and forks:periodic-note-prefix-match-setting describe the same prefix-matching feature family as pn:strict-then-prefix-date-parsing and pn:allow-prefix-match-gate, just observed from the other historical codebase; they are folded into the same story (US-FMT-04) rather than duplicated into a second one.

Most acceptance criteria in this epic are unit-testable in isolation (pure date math), which is why testable_by is almost always 'unit' rather than 'integration' or 'manual'; the two 'integration' criteria in US-FMT-04 are the ones that assert against the real shape of the user's existing vault, and the one 'manual' criterion in US-FMT-03 covers a live-reload UX check that is hard to assert purely in a unit test.

SET owns the settings UI for the format field, the prefix-match toggle, and the locale/week-start dropdowns; this epic owns only what those stored values must cause to happen. NOTE owns what happens once a note is found or not found (create, open, index); this epic only decides whether a given filename counts as a match. TPL owns the same {{weekday:fmt}} token syntax inside the note body; this epic owns only its use inside the filename format field, sharing the day-of-week resolution mechanism (dni:get-day-of-week-numerical-value) with TPL as a cross-epic dependency rather than a duplicated rule.
